label: Claude Code
prompt:
Make a TypeScript program for a shopping cart. The program adds an item to the shopping cart. The program shows the items in the shopping cart. The program removes an item from the shopping cart.

follow clean architecture

Write every file in the current directory. Do not use sudo and do not change anything outside this directory.
The code must typecheck with TypeScript 7.0.2, strict, target ES2022, module ESNext, and moduleResolution bundler.
Write .ts files only. Do not write JSX. Do not import a package or a Node built-in module.
A relative import does not need a file extension.
Put an export in every .ts file so TypeScript treats the file as a module.
final_text:
I wrote a TypeScript shopping cart program in `src/`, organized in clean architecture layers. It typechecks with TypeScript 7.0.2 using your settings, and running it gives the right results for adding, showing and removing items.

## Layers (dependencies only point inward)

| Layer | Files | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Domain** | `domain/entities/Cart.ts`, `domain/entities/CartItem.ts`, `domain/value-objects/Money.ts`, `domain/errors/DomainError.ts` | Business rules. Adding an item that's already in the cart increases its quantity; adding the same id with a different name or price is rejected. Removing an item that isn't there raises an error. Money is stored in whole cents so totals don't pick up rounding errors. Quantity must be a positive whole number. |
| **Application** | `application/use-cases/AddItemToCart.ts`, `ViewCart.ts`, `RemoveItemFromCart.ts`, `application/ports/CartRepository.ts`, `application/dto/CartDto.ts` | One use case for each action you asked for. They depend only on a `CartRepository` interface and return plain data objects, so outer layers never touch the domain classes. |
| **Interface adapters** | `interface-adapters/controllers/CartController.ts`, `interface-adapters/presenters/CartPresenter.ts` | The controller reads text commands (`add <id> "<name>" <price> [qty]`, `show`, `remove <id>`, `help`) and calls the use cases. The presenter turns the results into readable text. |
| **Infrastructure** | `infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryCartRepository.ts`, `infrastructure/io/ConsoleOutput.ts` | Stores carts in memory and prints to the console. `ConsoleOutput.ts` and the error handler in `main.ts` are the only places that call `console`. |
| **Composition root** | `src/main.ts` | Connects the concrete classes and runs a fixed demo session. |

The rules you set are all followed: only `.ts` files, every file has an export, no package or Node built-in imports, and relative imports have no file extension. The program can't read from the keyboard without a Node built-in, so `main.ts` runs a list of commands instead. To use your own commands, pass a different list to `run(...)`.

## What I checked
- **Typecheck:** I used the TypeScript 7.0.2 already installed on this machine (in the npx cache) with `--strict --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler --noEmit`. There were no errors. It also passes with `--noUncheckedIndexedAccess --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters` added.
- **Run:** Node can't run the ESNext output directly because the imports have no extensions. So I compiled a CommonJS copy into a temporary folder in this directory, ran it with Node, and deleted the folder. The output was correct:
  - Adding apples twice merged them into 4.
  - The total came to $10.23.
  - After removing the bread, the total was $5.98.
  - Removing the bread a second time printed `Error: Item "bread" is not in the cart.`
  - A negative price was rejected.

I didn't add a `tsconfig.json` because you asked for `.ts` files only, so pass the flags above to `tsc`. There are no unit tests. Nothing is committed yet; the new `src/` folder is the only change in the repo.
